Definition: The administration reported deploying at least the required share of the notified satellites (10% at M1, 50% at M2, 100% at M3) by this milestone, in every frequency band.
The required share was reached in some of the network's frequency bands but not in others.
The reported deployment was below the required share for this milestone.
The required share was not reached. Under resolves 12 of Resolution 35, the number of satellites recorded for the network is to be reduced in line with what was actually deployed.
The administration has sent its milestone report and the ITU has posted it as received, but the Radiocommunication Bureau has not yet examined and published it.
This milestone's deadline has not been reached yet.
This milestone's deadline has passed, but the Space Network List does not show a status for it yet.
There is no separate report for this milestone: a later milestone was already met (for example, 100% of the satellites were deployed at the first report).
Name of the satellite network (the ITU filing), e.g. STEAM-1. This is the filing's name, not an individual satellite's name, even though the SNL page heads the column 'Satellite Name'.
ITU country symbol of the notifying administration (the national regulator that submitted the filing), e.g. NOR, USA, G. ITU symbols are not ISO codes (D = Germany, G = United Kingdom).
English name of the country for the ADM symbol, from itu_country_codes.csv.
Symbol of the intergovernmental satellite organization that submitted the filing on behalf of its member administrations, if any (e.g. EUTELSAT, INTELSAT). Empty for all current Res 35 networks.

The later of (a) the end of the 7-year regulatory period for bringing the frequency assignments into use (RR No. 11.44) and (b) 1 January 2021. All milestone periods are counted from this date: M0 at +0, M1 at +2, M2 at +5 and M3 at +7 years.
Satellites the administration reported as deployed in the network's latest Res 35 report, out of the total number of satellites in its notified filing.
total_deployed / total_notified x 100. Calculated by us; the oldest PDFs print the same measure per frequency band.

Number the report gives each frequency band (1, 2, 3, ...). A frequency band is one continuous range of radio frequencies, from freq_min_mhz to freq_max_mhz. Numbers restart in every report, so band 1 in one PDF is not band 1 in another.

Lower edge of the frequency band, in megahertz (MHz): the lowest radio frequency in the range the network may use. 1,000 MHz = 1 GHz, so 17803.5 MHz is about 17.8 GHz. With freq_max_mhz it gives the full range of the band.
Upper edge of the frequency band, in megahertz (MHz): the highest radio frequency in the range the network may use. 1,000 MHz = 1 GHz. The band's width is freq_max_mhz minus freq_min_mhz.
